7. Now let us see what the prophetic spirit prays may fall upon them, rather foretelling than cursing. “Do thou to them,” he saith, “as unto Madian and Sisera, as unto Jabin at the brook of Kishon” (ver. 9). “They perished at Endor, they became as the dung of the earth” (ver. 10)
28. In the might of this Spirit, as we have it in the Book of Judges, Othniel judged Judges iii. 10.

And this was not without meaning; but that by means of the number of the ten men, See Judg. vi. 27. It is not very clear how Irenæus makes out this allegory, but it is thought that he refers to the initial letter in the name ᾽Ιησοῦς, which stands for ten in the Greek enumeration.
The little boy, therefore, who guided Samson by the hand, Judg. xvi. 26.
